items.title: IST DASLab publishes GSQ-RCO GGUFs of Inkling 2 Mini: the 26B looped MoE in about 10.5 GB at 3.5 bits per weight, retaining 99% of base scores
items.summary: Non-uniform GGUF quants of Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini at 2.75 to 3.5 bits per weight, with per-tensor precision picked by a gradient-based search, so the 26B looped MoE fits a 12 GB GPU in llama.cpp. The card reports AIME25, GPQA-Diamond and LiveCodeBench v6 against the base model.

doubt.pushback: Repliers note the 12 GB figure leaves little room for KV cache, ask which evals and context length back the 99% claim, and one cites unsourced talk that GSQ-RCO quants weaken long agent tasks.

reception.summary: Mostly enthusiasm about a 26B model on consumer GPUs, with questions on KV-cache headroom, Windows support and benchmark choice; one replier reports the earlier Qwen3.8 GSQ-RCO build worked well.

items.title: MiaAI Lab updates its TensorFold recipes for Inkling 2 Mini: DGX Spark decode up 21 to 35%, RTX 5090 and PRO 6000 up 43 to 66%
items.summary: New versions of MiaAI Lab's open run recipes raise single-stream Inkling 2 Mini decode on one DGX Spark from 48 to 64 tok/s and prefill from about 3.5k to 4.3k tok/s; the RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000 recipes reach 230 tok/s single stream and 679 tok/s at 8 streams. Directly useful for serving Inkling 2 Mini on a Spark.

doubt.pushback: Throughput numbers are self-reported by the recipe author, with no independent rerun yet.

items.title: Side-by-side on one RTX 5090: Inkling 2 Mini codes at 318.7 tok/s on Basalt, 205.1 on TensorFold and 111.1 on llama.cpp
items.summary: A builder ran three local engines on the same card and prompts: Basalt was fastest, TensorFold scored slightly higher on IFEval with similar overall quality, and llama.cpp could not hold 128K context with drafting on. A practical guide to picking a local engine for this model.

doubt.pushback: Single-machine run with no published harness; predates the latest TensorFold recipe update.

items.title: Omarchy 4.6 RC names the coding agent behind a root password prompt
items.summary: When an agent runs a pkexec command, the Omarchy polkit dialog now says which of 14 known agents (Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes and others) is asking, shows its icon and any reason it gave. It is a hint, not proof, since any program can claim a name; it ships in the 4.6.0 release candidate.

items.title: Sber releases GigaAM-v4 (238M) and GigaAM-Multilingual-v2 (776M) open ASR models under MIT
items.summary: Two small speech recognition models are on Hugging Face under MIT; Sber reports the 238M GigaAM-v4 beating Whisper large-v3 on the public Open ASR English subset and leading on Russian sets. A community MLX port for Apple silicon already exists.

doubt.pushback: WER comparisons are vendor-reported on the model card.

items.title: Tencent ships GGUF builds of Hy-MT3-30B-A3B, its 102-language translation MoE, for llama.cpp
items.summary: Official GGUF quantizations (down to IQ2) let the 3B-active translation model run locally in llama.cpp, so private on-device translation across 102 languages is now a download away.

items.title: Diffbot's 3-bit EXL3 pack runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at full 1M context on two RTX PRO 6000s with vLLM
items.summary: A 3 bpw EXL3 quant plus an optional CPU runtime keeps some routed experts in pinned host RAM so the full 1M context fits two 96 GB cards, with up to 289 tok/s reported on agentic coding.

doubt.pushback: Needs about 280 GB of free system RAM; speed figures are from the pack's own benchmarks.

items.title: Robbyant releases LingBot-Map 2.0 inference code and streaming base weights for frame-by-frame 3D reconstruction
items.summary: A causal streaming model predicts camera pose, intrinsics, depth and confidence as RGB frames arrive, runnable from a CLI or embedded per frame in an app. Code and weights are CC BY-NC 4.0, so noncommercial only.

items.title: DeepSeek ships DeepEP V2.6 and DeepEP-Ascend V1.1, plus fused Ascend kernels in FlashMLA
items.summary: DeepEP V2.6 adds buffer resizing, FP32 combine output and redundant-expert mapping; DeepEP-Ascend V1.1 drops the HCCL runtime dependency and adds cluster-scale training pieces; FlashMLA gains fused kernels and head128 support for Huawei Ascend. Open MoE serving and training code now targets Ascend 950 as well as NVIDIA SM100.

items.title: Ling 3.2 Air official FP8 (124B, 5.5B active) runs across two DGX Sparks with vLLM TP=2 at 47 tok/s single stream
items.summary: A builder split the 129 GB FP8 checkpoint over two linked Sparks with tensor parallelism and measured 47.11 tok/s with thinking on, after vLLM rejected the first two launch attempts. A data point for anyone sizing a two-Spark setup.

doubt.pushback: One run, one stream, launch flags not published in the post.
